summary: Parses the process command-line string (a2) for NetComm network options (--password, --dedicated, --host, --gamename, --connect, --name, --maxplayers) and populates a NetComm configuration object: host/connect flags, connect address buffer with a defaulted port, game name, player name, and a clamped maximum player count. Development logging is gated on dword_7C569C != 5 and a StringSplitLoop condition.

operations.description: If dword_7C569C != 5 and StringSplitLoop(1, aDDevF119992002_1, 6949) returns nonzero, enable the NetComm check-in debug log.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aNetcommCheckin) logs that NetComm command-line parsing is starting.
sub_566810(a2, aPassword) searches the command line for the password token; if absent, the password block is skipped.
sub_587DD0(v28, token_value + strlen(aPassword), 15) copies at most 15 characters of the password value into local buffer v28, then v28[15] = 0 terminates it.
sub_587C20(v28, asc_5C64D4) locates a separator character in the password buffer; if found, that position is zeroed to truncate the password.
StringCopyToStructField(v28) copies the parsed password into a configuration struct field managed by that routine.
If dword_7C569C != 5 and StringSplitLoop(1, aDDevF119992002_1, 6970) returns nonzero, enable the game-password debug log.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aSettingGamePas) logs that the game password is being set.
If sub_566810(a2, aDedicated) finds the dedicated token, the entire host/connect block is skipped: dedicated servers do not parse host or connect arguments.
If sub_566810(a2, aHost) finds the host token, parse host configuration; otherwise fall through to the connect branch.
Set the object byte field at offset 197 to 1, marking the session as host.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aNetcommActivat) logs that NetComm host mode is being activated.
If sub_566810(a2, aGamename) finds the game-name token, parse the game name.
sub_587DD0(v28, token_value + strlen(aGamename), 63) copies at most 63 characters of the game-name value into v28, then v28[63] = 0 terminates it.
sub_5897CA(v28, asc_5C64D4) cleans the game-name buffer; if the result is non-empty, strcpy copies it into the object buffer at offset 364.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aSettingGameNam) logs that the game name is being set.
If sub_566810(a2, aConnect) finds the connect token, parse the connect address and port.
sub_587DD0(object_buffer_at_offset_200, connect_value, 79) copies at most 79 characters of the connect argument into the object address buffer at offset 200, then the byte at +79 is zeroed.
Skip leading space characters and terminate the copied address buffer at the first space, leaving only the address portion.
sub_587C20(address_buffer, byte_5C3F6C) searches the address buffer for the port separator; returns a pointer to the separator or null.
If the separator is found, set the object byte field at offset 198 to 1, marking the session as an active client/connect.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aNetcommActivat_0) logs that NetComm connect mode is being activated.

If sub_587ECE(port_string) returns 0 (empty or non-numeric port), format the default port word_7D1004 as a string via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck(v28, "%d", word_7D1004) and strcpy it into the port portion of the address buffer.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aAutojoinAddres) logs the auto-join address default-port substitution.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aNewAddressStri) logs the new address string after the default port is appended.
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aNoPortSpecifie) logs that no port was specified in the connect argument.
If sub_566810(a2, aName_1) finds the player-name token, parse the player name.
Parse the player-name value: skip leading spaces; if the value is quoted, read until the closing quote, otherwise read until a space; copy at most 30 characters into v28 and NUL-terminate it.
If the parsed name buffer is non-empty, strcpy copies it into the object buffer at offset 284 (the player-name field).
DebugLogWrite(&dword_8AD25C, aNetcommSetNetw) logs that the network/player name was set.
If sub_566810(a2, aMaxplayers) finds the max-players token, parse the maximum player count.
Skip leading spaces in the max-players value, convert it with sub_587ECE, and store the result in the object dword field at offset 428.
Clamp the parsed max-players field to the range [2, 104]: values below 2 are raised to 2, values above 104 are lowered to 104.
Return result, the value left from the max-players parse (or null if the token was absent).
